parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows the prism $ABCDEF$ with cross section triangle $ABC$.

![q21-4ma1-1hr-qp-jan20-paper1-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/001-q21-4ma1-1hr-qp-jan20-paper1-igcse-maths.png)

Angle $BEC$= 40° and angle $ACB$is obtuse. $AC$ = 6 cm and $CE$= 13cm

The area of triangle $ABC$is 22 $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$

Calculate the length of $AB$. 
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

..................$\mathrm{cm}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Start by marking the given information on the diagram.*

![3d-trig-pythag-vh5-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/002-3d-trig-pythag-vh5-1.png)

> *We cannot assume that **BC** is 6 cm as we are not told that triangle **ABC **is isosceles. Therefore we need to use trigonometry with triangle **BCE **to find** BC**.*

$sin \left(40 \circ\right) = \frac{B C}{13}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 13 to find **BC.*

$B C = 13 sin \left(40 \circ\right) = 8 . 356 238 . . .$

*Store this result in your calculator to preserve accuracy in future calculations.* *Use this result and "*$\frac{1}{2}absinC$*" with the area of triangle **ABC** to find angle **C.*

$\frac{1}{2} \left(6\right) \left(8 . 356 238 . . .\right) sin C = 22$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to find angle **C.*

$\begin{aligned}sin C & = & \frac{22}{\frac{1}{2} \left(6\right) \left(8 . 356 238 . . .\right)} \\ C & = & sin^{- 1} \left(\frac{22}{\frac{1}{2} \left(6\right) \left(8 . 356 238 . . .\right)}\right) \\ C & = & 61 . 352 736 . . . \circ\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *We are told that angle **C **is obtuse, so subtract this acute answer from 180° to find the obtuse angle.*

$180^{\circ}-61.352736...^{\circ}=118.647263...^{\circ}$

**[1]**

> *Finally, use the cosine rule "*$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bccosA$*" with triangle **ACB** (we have two sides and the included angle) to find **AB*

$A B^{2} = 6^{2} + \left(8 . 356 . . .\right)^{2} - 2 \left(6\right) \left(8 . 356 . . .\right) c o s \left(118 . 647 . . . \circ\right)$

**[1]**

> *Evaluate and square root both sides to find **AB**.*

$\begin{aligned}A B & = & \sqrt{6^{2} + \left(8 . 356 . . .\right)^{2} - 2 \left(6\right) \left(8 . 356 . . .\right) c o s \left(118 . 647 . . . \circ\right)} \\ A B & = & 12 . 405 647 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round your answer to 1 decimal place as requested.*

**AB**** = 12.4 cm** **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
$ABC$ is an isosceles triangle in a horizontal plane. The point $T$ is vertically above $B$.

![q22-4ma1-2hr-qp-jan21-paper2-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/039-q22-4ma1-2hr-qp-jan21-paper2-igcse-maths.png)

Angle $ABC=140^{\circ}$
 $AB=BC=8cm$ 
$TB=10cm$ 
$M$ is the midpoint of $AC$.

Calculate the size of the angle between $MT$ and the horizontal plane $ABC$. 
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To find the angle between a line and a plane it is helpful to draw a right angled triangle using the line that is perpendicular to the plane:*

![iKy_xKdZ_3d-trig-pythag-h3-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/040-iky-xkdz-3d-trig-pythag-h3-1.png)

> *In order to find the required angle you will first need to find the length of the side **MB**.*

> *Triangle **ABC**  is isosceles as **AB **= **BC** = 8 cm. Therefore we can divide triangle **ABC** in two, to form two right-angle triangles. One of the right-angle triangles is shown below. Angle **ABC** is bisected so we know that angle **MBC** is 70°:*

![3d-trig-pythag-h3-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/041-3d-trig-pythag-h3-2.png)

> *Now we can find **MB** as we have an angle and a hypotenuse in a right-angle triangle. We need the adjacent side, so use the cosine ratio.*

$cos \left(70\right) = \frac{M B}{8}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 8*

$\begin{aligned}M B & = & 8 cos \left(70\right) \\ & = & 2 . 736161147 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *It's best to store this result as an exact value on your calculator. We can mark it on the diagram:*

![3d-trig-pythag-h3-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/042-3d-trig-pythag-h3-3.png)

> *Now we have two known sides on a right-angle triangle; the adjacent (2.736...) and the opposite (10, circled above). Use the tangent ratio to find the required angle.*

$\begin{aligned}tan \left(x\right) & = & \frac{10}{2 . 736 . . .}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Use the inverse tangent function ("SHIFT tan") on your calculator to find **x.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & tan^{- 1} \left(\frac{10}{2 . 736 . . .}\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Round your answer to 1 decimal place as requested. Remember to include the units.*

**Answer = 74.7°**  **[1]**

*ABCDEFGH* is a cuboid.

*CH* = 8.1 cm

parts.solutionMd:
> *To find the angle between a line and a plane it is helpful to draw a right angled triangle using the line that is perpendicular to the plane.*

![4-12-edexcel-gcse-hq1-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/073-4-12-edexcel-gcse-hq1-1.png)

> *In order to find the required angle you will first need to find the length of the side **AC**. To do this draw a right angled triangle using the other information you are given.*

![7hiOPm-A_4-12-edexcel-gcse-hq1-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/074-7hiopm-a-4-12-edexcel-gcse-hq1-2.png)

> *In the triangle **ABC** you know an angle and the length of the side opposite. You want to find the hypotenuse so use the sin ratio.*

$sin \left(48\right) = \frac{7 . 3}{x}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by **x** and divide by sin(48).*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{7 . 3}{sin \left(48\right)} \\ & = & 9 . 823118 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Now you can use the triangle **CAH**. In this triangle you want to find an angle and you know the lengths of the sides that are opposite and adjacent to the angle so use the tan ratio. Use the answer button or the exact value for the length of the side **AC**.*

$tan \left(x\right) = \frac{8 . 1}{9 . 823118 . . .}$

**[1]**

> *Find the angle by using the inverse tan function.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & tan^{- 1} \left(\frac{8 . 1}{9 . 823118 . . .}\right) \\ & = & 39 . 508492 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round your answer to 1 decimal place. Remember to include the units.*

$\mathrm{Angle} \mathrm{between}AH\mathrm{and} \mathrm{the} \mathrm{plane}ABCD=39.5^{\circ}(1\mathrm{dp})$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a solid prism $ABCDEFGH$.

![q17-4ma1-2h-qp-jan21-paper2-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/007-q17-4ma1-2h-qp-jan21-paper2-igcse-maths.png)

The trapezium $ABCD$, in which $AD$ is parallel to $BC$, is a cross section of the prism. 
The base $ADEH$ of the prism is a horizontal plane. $ADEH$ and $BCFG$ are rectangles. 
The midpoint of $BC$ is vertically above the midpoint of $AD$ so that $BA=CD$.

$AD=37\mathrm{cm}$   $GF=28\mathrm{cm}$    $DE=24\mathrm{cm}$

The perpendicular distance between edges $AD$ and $BC$ is 20 $\mathrm{cm}$.

Calculate the size of the angle between $AF$ and the plane $ADEH$. 
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To identify the angle between a line and a plane it is helpful to draw a right angled triangle using **AD** and the line that is perpendicular to the plane:*

![4sE77S~X_3d-trig-pythag-vh4-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/008-4se77s-x-3d-trig-pythag-vh4-1.png)

> *We have added **K **to the diagram. To find **x**, we need to obtain the length **AK **so we can consider triangle **AHK**:*

![6Ns9D~M-_3d-trig-pythag-vh4-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/009-6ns9d-m-3d-trig-pythag-vh4-2.png)

> *In right-angle triangle **AHK**, we already have length **AH** so to find **AK** we need length **HK.** We can deduce **HK** by considering trapezium **EFGH**:*

![AIya-JbQ_3d-trig-pythag-vh4-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/010-aiya-jbq-3d-trig-pythag-vh4-3.png)

$HL=KE\mathrm{and}HL+KE=37-28\,KE=\frac{37-28}{2}=4.5\,HK=37-4.5=32.5$

> *Now we can find **AK **using Pythagoras' Theorem in triangle **AHK **(our second diagram).*

$\begin{aligned}A K & = & \sqrt{A H^{2} + H K^{2}} \\ & = & \sqrt{24^{2} + 32 . 5^{2}} \\ & = & 40 . 40111385 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *(This mark was hard won! But the remaining two marks are now close!)*

> *Save this result in your calculator to preserve accuracy. *
*Find **x** using triangle **AFK **(our first diagram) and the tangent ratio.*

$tan \left(x\right) = \frac{20}{40 . 40111385 . . .}$

**[1]**

> *Use the inverse tangent function ("SHIFT tan" on your calculator) to find the required angle.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & tan^{- 1} \left(\frac{20}{40 . 40111385 . . .}\right) \\ & = & 26 . 33706009 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round your answer to 1 decimal place as requested. Remember to include the units.*

**Answer = **$26.3^{\circ}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a triangular prism $ABCDEF$ with a horizontal base $ABEF$.

![q22-4ma1-1h-qp-june21-paper1-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/032-q22-4ma1-1h-qp-june21-paper1-igcse-maths.png)

$AC=BC=FD=ED=12\mathrm{cm}$       $AB=10\mathrm{cm}$           $BE=15\mathrm{cm}$

Calculate the size of the angle between $AD$ and the base $ABEF$. 
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To identify the angle between a line and a plane it is helpful to draw a right angled triangle using **AD **and the line that is perpendicular to the plane:*

![3d-trig-pythag-vh3-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/033-3d-trig-pythag-vh3-1.png)

> *Triangle** EDF** is isosceles so **M** is the midpoint of **FE. **In order to find the required angle we need to find two lengths on triangle **AMD**. We will find **DM** and **AM** as follows.*

> *We can draw two new right-angle triangles to help us find sides **DM** and **AM **as below. Because **M **is the midpoint of **FE**, we know that **FM **= **ME **= 5cm.*

![3d-trig-pythag-vh3-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/034-3d-trig-pythag-vh3-2.png)

> *We can see from the diagrams that to find **DM** and **AM**, we can use Pythagoras' Theorem with two different triangles.*

$DM=\sqrt{12^{2}-5^{2}}=\sqrt{119}$

**[1]**

$AM=\sqrt{15^{2}+5^{2}}=5\sqrt{10}$

**[1]**

> *We can mark these results on our diagram:*

![3d-trig-pythag-vh3-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/035-3d-trig-pythag-vh3-3.png)

> *Now we have the opposite and adjacent side so can use the tangent ratio to find the required angle*

$\begin{aligned}tan \left(x\right) & = & \frac{\sqrt{119}}{5 \sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Use the inverse tangent function ("SHIFT tan" on your calculator) to find the required angle*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & tan^{- 1} \left(\frac{\sqrt{119}}{5 \sqrt{10}}\right) \\ & = & 34 . 60286258 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round your answer to 3 significant figures as requested. Remember to include the units.*

**Answer = **$34.6^{\circ}$ **[1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *To identify the angle between a line and a plane it is helpful to draw a right angled triangle using the line that is perpendicular to the plane:*

![3d-trig-pythag-m2-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/067-3d-trig-pythag-m2-1.png)

> *We need to find angle **x**. Notice that we have side **AE.** In order to find the required angle we first need to find the length of the side **AC**. To do this draw a right angled triangle connecting hypotenuse **AC** with sides whose lengths are known:*

![3d-trig-pythag-m2-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/068-3d-trig-pythag-m2-2.png)

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows the prism $ABCDEFGHJK$ with horizontal base $AEFG$

![q21-january-2022-1h-edexcel-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/013-q21-january-2022-1h-edexcel-igcse-maths.png)

$ABCDE$ is a cross section of the prism where

$ABDE$ is a square 
$BCD$ is an equilateral triangle

$EF=2\timesAE$  
$M$is the midpoint of $GF$ so that $JM$ is vertical.

Angle $MAJ=y^{\circ}$ 
Given that            $\mathrm{tan}y^{\circ}=T$ 
find the value of$T$, giving your answer in the form $\frac{\sqrt{p}+\sqrt{q}}{17}$ where $p$ and $q$ are integers.

$T$ = ...........................
parts.solutionMd:
> *Start by marking the information given on the diagram. We don't know any lengths but we can assign arbitray values so long as they are kept in the given ratios. *
*We can start by labeling the smallest known segments, **GM **and **MF**, as** **"1". *
*We can also mark angle **MAJ** as **y**.*

![3d-trig-pythag-vh6-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/014-3d-trig-pythag-vh6-1.png)

> *To find **y**, we need to find two lengths on triangle **AJM**. *

> *First, we will find **AM**.*

> *If **GM **= **MF **= 1 then **GF **= 2 so **AE **= 2.  *
*From the question**, EF** = 2 × **AE** so **EF** = **AG **= 4.*

![3d-trig-pythag-vh6-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/015-3d-trig-pythag-vh6-2.png)

> *Using Pythagoras' Theorem with triangle **AGM**, we can find **AM**. *

$\begin{aligned}A M & = & \sqrt{1^{2} + 4^{2}} \\ & = & \sqrt{1 + 16} \\ & = & \sqrt{17}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Now we turn our attention to finding **MJ**.*

> *Add a point **N** to the line **HK** directly above **M**. Triangle **HJK** is equilateral so **NK** = 1 and **JK **= 2:*

![v-JQcpZB_3d-trig-pythag-vh6-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/016-v-jqcpzb-3d-trig-pythag-vh6-3.png)

> *Using Pythagoras' Theorem with triangle **JKN, **we can find **JN*

$\begin{aligned}J N & = & \sqrt{2^{2} - 1^{2}} \\ & = & \sqrt{4 - 1} \\ & = & \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *We add **MN** and **JN** to get **MJ.*

$\begin{aligned}M J & = & \sqrt{3} + 2\end{aligned}$

> *Mark **MJ **and **AM** on triangle **AMJ.*

![3d-trig-pythag-vh6-4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/017-3d-trig-pythag-vh6-4.png)

> *Now we can use trigonometry with triangle** AMJ** to find the value of tan(y), or **T**.*

$\begin{aligned}T & = & tan \left(y\right) = \frac{\sqrt{3} + 2}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Finally we need to rationalise the denominator*

$\begin{aligned}T & = & \frac{\sqrt{17} \left(\sqrt{3} + 2\right)}{\sqrt{17} \sqrt{17}} \\ & = & \frac{\sqrt{51} + 2 \sqrt{17}}{17}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *We are almost there! We need to write the answer in the form requested. 2 is the same as √4 so...*

$\begin{aligned} & = & \frac{\sqrt{51} + \sqrt{4} \sqrt{17}}{17} \\ & = & \frac{\sqrt{51} + \sqrt{68}}{17}\end{aligned}$

$\mathbf{\mathit{T}} \begin{aligned} & = & \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & \frac{\sqrt{51} + \sqrt{68}}{17}\end{aligned}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a prism $ABCDEFGH$ with a horizontal base.

![q17-paper1hr-nov2020-edexcel-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/043-q17-paper1hr-nov2020-edexcel-igcse-maths.png)

The base of the prism, $EFGH$, is a square of side $12\mathrm{cm}.$ Trapezium $ADEF$ is a cross section of the prism where $AF$ and $DE$ are vertical edges.

$\begin{aligned}D E & = & C H = 10 cm \\ A D & = & B C = 15 cm\end{aligned}$

Work out the size of the angle between $CF$ and the base $EFGH.$ 
Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Look at the base from above and find the length **FH** using Pythagoras' theorem on the right-angled triangle **FHE**.*

![edexcel-igcse-3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry-h-q6a-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/044-edexcel-igcse-3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry-h-q.png)

$\begin{aligned}x^{2} & = & 12^{2} + 12^{2} \\ x^{2} & = & 288 \\ x & = & \sqrt{288}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Use trigonometry on the right-angled triangle **FCH**. *

> *You know the opposite side and the adjacent side, so use *$\mathrm{tan}θ=\frac{Opp}{Adj}$*.*

![edexcel-igcse-3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry-h-q6a-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/trigonometry/3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/045-edexcel-igcse-3d-pythagoras-and-trigonometry-h-q.png)

parts.solutionMd:
> *Draw the stick on the diagram such that it extends from a bottom corner through the diagonally opposite top corner and out of the crate.  *

$\begin{aligned}46^{2} + 46^{2} & = & c^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}c^{2} & = & 2 \left(46^{2}\right) \\ & = & 4232 \\ c & = & \sqrt{4232} \\ & = & 46 \sqrt{2} cm\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Use Pythagoras' theorem on the right-angled triangle made up of the diagonal at the base, the side with length 55 cm and the diagonal made by the part of the stick inside the crate, **x.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(46 \sqrt{2}\right)^{2} + 55^{2} & = & x^{2} \\ 4232 + 3025 & = & x^{2} \\ x^{2} & = & 7257 \\ x & = & \sqrt{7257} cm\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Calculate the length of the stick that extends out of the crate by subtracting **x** from the length of the stick.*

$\begin{aligned}95 - x & = & 95 - \sqrt{7257} \\ & = & 95 - 85 . 188027 . . . \end{aligned}$

$9.81\mathrm{cm}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
$2-\frac{x+2}{x-3}-\frac{x-6}{x+3}$  can be written as a single fraction in the form $\frac{ax+b}{x^{2}-9}$

where $a$and $b$ are integers.

Work out the value of $a$ and the value of $b$.
parts.solutionMd:
*Think of 2 as the fraction *$\frac{2}{1}$

$\frac{2}{1}-\frac{x+2}{x-3}-\frac{x-6}{x+3}$

*Find the lowest common denominator of 1, (**x** - 3) and (**x** + 3) by multiplying them together* * *

*lowest common denominator is *$\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)$

**[1]**

*Multiply top-and-bottom of each fraction by the brackets needed to form this denominator* * *

$\frac{2 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)}{\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{\left(x + 2\right) \left(x + 3\right)}{\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)} - \frac{\left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 6\right)}{\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)}$ * *

*Write as one single fraction over the common denominator Subtract the numerators* * *

$\frac{2 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right) - \left(x + 2\right) \left(x + 3\right) - \left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 6\right)}{\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)}$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets in the numerator (keeping their results in brackets)* * *

$\frac{2 \left(x^{2} - 9\right) - \left(x^{2} + 5 x + 6\right) - \left(x^{2} - 9 x + 18\right)}{\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)}$

> * *

*Expand the next layer of brackets (being careful to multiply all terms by -1 in the second and third brackets)* * *

$\frac{2 x^{2} - 18 - x^{2} - 5 x - 6 - x^{2} + 9 x - 18}{\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)}$ * *

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator  *

$\frac{4 x - 42}{\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)}$

**[1]**

> *This is not yet in the form *$\frac{ax+b}{x^{2}-9}$*  Expand the brackets in the denominator   *

> $\frac{4x-42}{x^{2}-9}$*  *

> *This is now in the form *$\frac{ax+b}{x^{2}-9}$* where **a **and **b** are integers (whole numbers)  *

**a*** = 4 and ***b*** = - 42*

$\frac{4x-42}{x^{2}-9}$* ***where ****a**** = 4 and ****b**** = - 42 ****[1]**

parts.problemMd: Simplify fully     $\frac{2x^{2}-5x+3}{x^{2}+5x-6}$
parts.solutionMd:
*"Simplify" for algebraic fractions means factorise and cancel* *Factorise the easier quadratic on the denominator * * *

$\frac{2 x^{2} - 5 x + 3}{\left(x + 6\right) \left(x - 1\right)}$

**[1]**

*The harder quadratic on the numerator is likely to have (**x** + 6) or (**x** - 1) as a factor* *Try factorising with (**x** + 6)* * *

$2 x^{2} - 5 x + 3 = \left(2 x \pm . . .\right) \left(x + 6\right) ?$ * *

*No whole number in the first bracket can complete this factorisation* *Try factorising with (**x** - 1)* * *

$2 x^{2} - 5 x + 3 = \left(2 x \pm . . .\right) \left(x - 1\right) ?$ * *

*The whole number -3 in the first bracket would multiply by -1 in the second bracket to give +3 on the left* * *

$2 x^{2} - 5 x + 3 = \left(2 x - 3\right) \left(x - 1\right)$

**[1]**

*This factorisation is now correct (expand and check)* *Cancel common brackets from top-and-bottom* * *

$\frac{\left(2 x - 3\right) \cancel{\left(x - 1\right)}}{\left(x + 6\right) \cancel{\left(x - 1\right)}}$

$\frac{2x-3}{x+6}$* ***[1]**

*Write as one single fraction over the common denominator Subtract the numerators* * *

$\frac{2 \left(y - 6\right) - \left(y + 3\right)}{\left(y + 3\right) \left(y - 6\right)}$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets in the numerator* * *

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator*

$\frac{y-15}{(y+3)(y-6)}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Show that $\frac{1}{6x^{2}+7x-5}\div\frac{1}{4x^{2}-1}$ simplifies to $\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}$ where $a,b,c$ and $d$ are integers.
parts.solutionMd:
*Dividing by *$\frac{a}{b}$* is the same as multiplying by *$\frac{b}{a}$

*Flip the second fraction and change ÷ into ×* * *

$\frac{1}{6x^{2}+7x-5}\times\frac{4x^{2}-1}{1}$ * *

*"Simplify" for algebraic fractions means factorise and cancel* *Factorise the numerator of the second fraction using the "difference of two squares" **a*<sup>*2*</sup>* - **b*<sup>*2*</sup>* = (**a **+ **b**)(**a **- **b**)   *

$\begin{aligned}4 x^{2} - 1 & = & \left(2 x\right)^{2} - 1^{2} \\ & = & \left(2 x + 1\right) \left(2 x - 1\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]*** *

*The calculation is now*

$\frac{1}{6 x^{2} + 7 x - 5} \times \frac{\left(2 x + 1\right) \left(2 x - 1\right)}{1}$

> *The harder quadratic on the denominator is likely to have (2**x** + 1) or (2**x** - 1) as a factor*

*Try factorising with (2**x** + 1)* * *

$6 x^{2} + 7 x - 5 = \left(3 x \pm . . .\right) \left(2 x + 1\right) ?$ * *

> *The whole number -5 in the first bracket would multiply by +1 in the second bracket to give -5 on the left *

*But expanding this attempt gives an incorrect middle term* * *

> $\left(3 x - 5\right) \left(2 x + 1\right) = 6 x^{2} \underline{- 7 x} - 5$*  *

*Try factorising with (2**x** - 1)* * *

$6 x^{2} + 7 x - 5 = \left(3 x \pm . . .\right) \left(2 x - 1\right) ?$ * *

> *The whole number +5 in the first bracket would multiply by -1 in the second bracket to give -5 on the left *

*Expanding this attempt shows it is correct* * *

$\left(3 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 1\right) = 6 x^{2} + 7 x - 5$

**[1]**

*Cancel common brackets from top-and-bottom (this is possible across the × sign)* * *

> $\frac{1}{\left(3 x + 5\right) \cancel{\left(2 x - 1\right)}} \times \frac{\left(2 x + 1\right) \cancel{\left(2 x - 1\right)}}{1}$*  *

> *Combine into one single fraction by multiplying the numerators together and multiplying the denominators together *

> *This is now in the form *$\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}$* where **a**, **b**, **c** and **d** are integers (whole numbers)*

$\frac{2x+1}{3x+5}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Simplify fully       $\frac{3-x}{3x^{2}-5x-12}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Simplify for algebraic fractions means factorise and cancel *

*To factorise the denominator, first multiply 3 by -12*

*3 × -12 = -36*

*Find two numbers that multiply to give -36 and add to give -5 (the middle number)*

*-9 and 4*

*Split the middle term into -9**x** and 4**x*

$3x^{2}-9x+4x-12$

*Factorise fully the first pair of terms and the second pair of terms *

$3 x \left(x - 3\right) + 4 \left(x - 3\right)$

*Factorise out the whole (**x** - 3) bracket as if it were one term, leaving 3**x** and +4 in their own bracket*

$\left(x - 3\right) \left(3 x + 4\right)$

**[1]**

> *Write the fraction with the denominator factorised  *

> $\frac{3 - x}{\left(x - 3\right) \left(3 x + 4\right)}$*  *

> *The 3 - **x** almost cancels with the **x** - 3 but the signs are wrong*

> * A good trick here is to factorise out -1 from 3 - **x**  *

> $3 - x = - 1 \left(- 3 + x\right)$*  *

> *Reorder the two terms inside the bracket (write the **x** first)  *

> $3 - x = - 1 \left(x - 3\right)$*  *

> *Write the algebraic fraction with this new form of the numerator  *

> $\frac{- 1 \left(x - 3\right)}{\left(x - 3\right) \left(3 x + 4\right)}$*  *

> *The brackets can now be more clearly cancelled on top-and-bottom  *

$\frac{- 1 \cancel{\left(x - 3\right)}}{\cancel{\left(x - 3\right)} \left(3 x + 4\right)}$

$\frac{-1}{3x+4}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Write $\frac{x}{x-1}-\frac{x}{x+1}$ as a single fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
*Find the lowest common denominator by multiplying (**x** - 1) by (**x** + 1)* * *

*lowest common denominator is *$\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 1\right)$

**[1]**

*Multiply top-and-bottom of each fraction by the brackets needed to form this denominator* * *

$\frac{x \left(x + 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 1\right)} - \frac{x \left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 1\right)}$ * *

*Write as one single fraction over the common denominator Subtract the numerators* * *

$\frac{x \left(x + 1\right) - x \left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 1\right)}$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets in the numerator* * *

$\frac{x^{2} + x - x^{2} + x}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 1\right)}$ * *

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator*

$\frac{2x}{(x-1)(x+1)}$* ***[1]**

*"Simplify" for algebraic fractions means factorise and cancel* *Factorise the easier quadratic in the numerator, using the "difference of two squares" **a*<sup>*2*</sup>* - **b*<sup>*2*</sup>* = (**a **+ **b**)(**a **- **b**)* * *

$\frac{\left(x + 4\right) \left(x - 4\right)}{2 x^{2} - 5 x - 12}$

**[1]**

*The harder quadratic on the numerator is likely to have (**x** + 4) or (**x** - 4) as a factor*

*Try factorising with (**x** + 4)* * *

$2 x^{2} - 5 x - 12 = \left(2 x \pm . . .\right) \left(x + 4\right) ?$ * *

> *The whole number -3 in the first bracket would multiply by +4 in the second bracket to give -12 on the left *

*But expanding this attempt gives an incorrect middle term* * *

> $\left(2 x - 3\right) \left(x + 4\right) = 2 x^{2} \underline{+ 5 x} - 12$*  *

*Try factorising with (**x** - 4)* * *

$2 x^{2} - 5 x - 12 = \left(2 x \pm . . .\right) \left(x - 4\right) ?$ * *

> *The whole number +3 in the first bracket would multiply by -4 in the second bracket to give -12 on the left *

*Expanding this attempt shows it is correct* * *

$\left(2 x + 3\right) \left(x - 4\right) = 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 12$

**[1]**

*Cancel common brackets from top-and-bottom* * *

$\frac{\left(x + 4\right) \cancel{\left(x - 4\right)}}{\left(2 x + 3\right) \cancel{\left(x - 4\right)}}$

$\frac{x+4}{2x+3}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Express

$\frac{3}{x}+\frac{x+2}{2x}+\frac{1}{4}$

as a single fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *First we need the lowest common denominator (lcd) of **x**, 2**x** and 4.*

$\mathrm{lcd} \mathrm{of}x,2x\mathrm{and}4=4x$

> *Rewrite each fraction over the lcd.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{x} & = & \frac{3 \times 4}{4 x} = \frac{12}{4 x} \\ \frac{x + 2}{2 x} & = & \frac{\left(x + 2\right) \times 2}{4 x} = \frac{2 x + 4}{4 x} \\ \frac{1}{4} & = & \frac{1 \times x}{4 x} = \frac{x}{4 x}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Now add the fractions by adding the numerators over a the single (lcd) denominator.*

$\frac{12}{4x}+\frac{2x+4}{4x}+\frac{x}{4x}=\frac{12+2x+4+x}{4x}$

**[1]**

> *Collect like terms (on the numerator) and simplify if possible.*

$\frac{12+2x+4+x}{4x}=\frac{3x+16}{4x}$

> *This cannot be simplified.*

$\therefore\frac{3}{x}+\frac{x+2}{2x}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{3x+16}{4x}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Write $\frac{25 x^{2} - 64}{5 x^{2} - 13 x - 6} \times \frac{x^{2} - 8 x + 15}{5 x + 8} - \left(x - 7\right)$

as a single fraction in its simplest form.

Show clear algebraic working.
parts.solutionMd:
> *The two fractions are being multiplied and involve three quadratic expressions.*

> * Factorise these expressions as this will make them easier to multiply.*

$\begin{aligned}25 x^{2} - 64 & = & \left(5 x - 8\right) \left(5 x + 8\right) \\ 5 x^{2} - 13 x - 6 & = & \left(5 x + 2\right) \left(x - 3\right) \\ x^{2} - 8 x + 15 & = & \left(x - 5\right) \left(x - 3\right)\end{aligned}$

**One quadratic correctly factorise****d [1]**
**Two quadratics correctly factorised**** [1]**

> *Rewrite the product of the fractions.*

$\frac{25 x^{2} - 64}{5 x^{2} - 13 x - 6} \times \frac{x^{2} - 8 x + 15}{5 x + 8} = \frac{\left(5 x - 8\right) \left(5 x + 8\right)}{\left(5 x + 2\right) \left(x - 3\right)} \times \frac{\left(x - 5\right) \left(x - 3\right)}{\left(5 x + 8\right)}$

> *Look to cancel any factors before multiplying.*

$\frac{\left(5 x - 8\right) \cancel{\left(5 x + 8\right)}}{\left(5 x + 2\right) \bcancel{\left(x - 3\right)}} \times \frac{\left(x - 5\right) \bcancel{\left(x - 3\right)}}{\cancel{\left(5 x + 8\right)}} = \frac{\left(5 x - 8\right) \left(x - 5\right)}{\left(5 x + 2\right)}$

> *Now we need to include the third term, *$- \left(x - 7\right)$*, and make a common denominator.*

$\frac{\left(5 x - 8\right) \left(x - 5\right)}{\left(5 x + 2\right)} - \left(x - 7\right) = \frac{\left(5 x - 8\right) \left(x - 5\right) - \left(x - 7\right) \left(5 x + 2\right)}{\left(5 x + 2\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Expand and simplify the numerator.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{\left(5 x - 8\right) \left(x - 5\right) - \left(x - 7\right) \left(5 x + 2\right)}{\left(5 x + 2\right)} & = & \frac{5 x^{2} - 33 x + 40 - \left(5 x^{2} - 33 x - 14\right)}{\left(5 x + 2\right)} \\ & = & \frac{5 x^{2} - 33 x + 40 - 5 x^{2} + 33 x + 14}{\left(5 x + 2\right)} \\ & = & \frac{54}{\left(5 x + 2\right)}\end{aligned}$

> *Nothing else can be simplified or cancelled.*

$\frac{25x^{2}-64}{5x^{2}-13x-6}\times\frac{x^{2}-8x+15}{5x+8}=\frac{54}{5x+2}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Show that  $\frac{a}{b + 1} - \frac{a}{\left(b + 1\right)^{2}}$ can be written as  $\frac{a b}{\left(b + 1\right)^{2}}$
parts.solutionMd:
*The lowest common denominator of (**b** + 1) and (**b** + 1)*<sup>*2*</sup>* is (**b **+ 1)*<sup>*2*</sup>* For example, the lowest common denominator of 3 and 9 is 9* * *

*lowest common denominator is** *$\left(b + 1\right)^{2}$ * *

*Multiply the top-and-bottom of the first fraction by (**b** + 1)*

$\frac{a \left(b + 1\right)}{\left(b + 1\right)^{2}} - \frac{a}{\left(b + 1\right)^{2}}$

*Write as one single fraction over the common denominator Subtract the numerators* * *

$\frac{a \left(b + 1\right) - a}{\left(b + 1\right)^{2}}$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets in the numerator* * *

$\frac{a b + a - a}{\left(b + 1\right)^{2}}$ * *

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator*

$\frac{ab}{(b+1)^{2}}$* ***[1***]*

parts.problemMd:
Express $\frac{4}{x-2}-\frac{3}{x+1}$ as a single fraction.

Give your answer in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *First we need the lowest common denominator (lcd) of **x **- 2 and **x** + 1. *
*Since these share no common factors, the lcd will be their product.*

$lcd of x - 2 and x + 1 = \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)$

> *Rewrite each fraction over the lcd.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{x - 2} & = & \frac{4 \left(x + 1\right)}{\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)} \\ \frac{3}{x + 1} & = & \frac{3 \left(x - 2\right)}{\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Now subtract the fractions by subtracting the numerators over the denominator (lcd).*

$\frac{4}{\left(x - 2\right)} - \frac{3}{\left(x + 1\right)} = \frac{4 \left(x + 1\right) - 3 \left(x - 2\right)}{\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)}$

> *Expand the brackets on the numerator and collect like terms.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{4 \left(x + 1\right) - 3 \left(x - 2\right)}{\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)} & = & \frac{4 x + 4 - 3 x + 6}{\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)} \\ & = & \frac{x + 10}{\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *This cannot be simplified.*

$\therefore\frac{4}{x-2}-\frac{3}{x+1}=\frac{x+10}{(x-2)(x+1)}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Given that  $x=\frac{5}{9y+5}$ and that $y=\frac{5}{5a-2}$

find an expression for $x$ in terms of $a$.

Give your expression as a single fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Substitute the second equation into the the first.*

$x = \frac{5}{9 \left(\frac{5}{5 a - 2}\right) + 5}$

**[1]**

> *Work carefully as you will be dealing with fractions within fractions - to deal with this you can write the 'main' fraction as a division statement, as below.*

$x = 5 \div \left[9 \left(\frac{5}{5 a - 2}\right) + 5\right]$

> *Multiply out the (round) brackets.*

$x = 5 \div \left[\frac{45}{5 a - 2} + 5\right]$

> *Make a common denominator within the square brackets.*

$x = 5 \div \left[\frac{45 + 5 \left(5 a - 2\right)}{5 a - 2}\right]$

**[1]**

> *Simplify the numerator.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & 5 \div \left[\frac{45 + 25 a - 10}{5 a - 2}\right] \\ x & = & 5 \div \left[\frac{35 + 25 a}{5 a - 2}\right] \\ x & = & 5 \div \left[\frac{5 \left(7 + 5 a\right)}{5 a - 2}\right]\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *This is 'dividing by a fraction' so use the shortcut of switching ÷ to × and flipping the (second) fraction.*

$x = \cancel{5} \\times \frac{5 a - 2}{ \cancel{5} ( 7 + 5 a )}$
$x = \frac{5 a - 2}{7 + 5 a}$

> *There isn't anything else that can be simplified or cancelled.*

$x=\frac{5a-2}{7+5a}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Simplify      $\frac{x^{2}-9}{2x^{2}+5x-3}$
parts.solutionMd:
*"Simplify" for algebraic fractions means factorise and cancel* *Factorise the easier quadratic in the numerator, using the "difference of two squares" **a*<sup>*2*</sup>* - **b*<sup>*2*</sup>* = (**a **+ **b**)(**a **- **b**)* * *

$\frac{\left(x + 3\right) \left(x - 3\right)}{2 x^{2} + 5 x - 3}$

**[1]**

*The harder quadratic on the numerator is likely to have (**x** + 3) or (**x** - 3) as a factor*

*Try factorising with (**x** + 3)* * *

$2 x^{2} + 5 x - 3 = \left(2 x \pm . . .\right) \left(x + 3\right) ?$ * *

> *The whole number -1 in the first bracket would multiply by +3 in the second bracket to give -3 on the left *

*Expanding this attempt shows it is correct* * *

$\left(2 x - 1\right) \left(x + 3\right) = 2 x^{2} + 5 x - 3$

**[1]**

*Cancel common brackets from top-and-bottom* * *

$\frac{\cancel{\left(x + 3\right)} \left(x - 3\right)}{\left(2 x - 1\right) \cancel{\left(x + 3\right)}}$

$\frac{x-3}{2x-1}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Write $\frac{2x+1}{4}+\frac{x-2}{3}$ as a single fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Find the lowest common denominator by multiplying 4 by 3*

*lowest common denominator is 4 × 3 = 12*

> *Multiply top-and-bottom of each fraction by the numbers needed to form this denominator*

$\frac{3 \left(2 x + 1\right)}{12} + \frac{4 \left(x - 2\right)}{12}$

**[1]**

> *Write as one single fraction over the common denominator Add the numerators*

$\frac{3 \left(2 x + 1\right) + 4 \left(x - 2\right)}{12}$

> *Expand the brackets in the numerator*

> $\frac{6x+3+4x-8}{12}$* *

**[1]**

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator*

$\frac{10x-5}{12}$

> *Check for anything that can be factorised and/or cancelled In this case the numerator has a factor of 2*

$\frac{5(2x-1)}{12}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Express  $\frac{1}{9x^{2}-25}-\frac{1}{6x+10}$ as a single fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Start by factorsing the (numerators and) denominators. *

> *Spot that the denominator on the left-hand side is the difference of two squares.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{9 x^{2} - 25} & = & \frac{1}{\left(3 x - 5\right) \left(3 x + 5\right)} \\ \frac{1}{6 x + 10} & = & \frac{1}{2 \left(3 x + 5\right)}\end{aligned}$

> *Now look for the lowest common denominator (lcd) of (3**x** - 5)(3**x** + 5) and 2(3**x** + 5).*

*lcd of (3***x*** - 5)(3***x*** + 5) and 2(3***x*** + 5) is 2(3***x*** + 5)(3***x*** - 5)*

> *Write the difference over a single denominator.*

$\frac{1}{9 x^{2} - 25} - \frac{1}{6 x + 10} = \frac{1 \times 2 - 1 \times \left(3 x - 5\right)}{2 \left(3 x + 5\right) \left(3 x - 5\right)}$

> *Simplify the numerator.*

$\frac{1}{9x^{2}-25}-\frac{1}{6'+10}=\frac{7-3x}{2(3x+5)(3x-5)}$

> *Check to see if anything cancels or simplifies further.*

*In this case nothing else does.*

$\frac{1}{9x^{2}-25}-\frac{1}{6x+10}=\frac{7-3x}{2(3x+5)(3x-5)}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Solve $\frac{4-3x}{5}-\frac{3x-5}{2}=-3$

Show clear algebraic working.

$x$ = .......................
parts.solutionMd:
> *First make a common denominator of the left-hand side of the equation. *
*For this we want the lowest common denominator (lcd) of 5 and 2.*

$\mathrm{lcd} \mathrm{of}5\mathrm{and}2=10$

> *Rewrite the left-hand side of the equation as a single fraction over the lcd and simplify the numerator.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{4 - 3 x}{5} - \frac{3 x - 5}{2} & = & \frac{2 \left(4 - 3 x\right) - 5 \left(3 x - 5\right)}{10} \\ & = & \frac{8 - 6 x - 15 x + 25}{10} \\ & = & \frac{33 - 21 x}{10}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Now bring the right-hand side of the equation in and multiply through by 10 to remove the fraction.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{33 - 21 x}{10} & = & - 3 \\ 33 - 21 x & = & - 30\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Solve this linear equation to find **x**.*

$\begin{aligned}33 - 21 x & = & - 30 \\ 21 x & = & 33 + 30 \\ 21 x & = & 63 \\ x & = & 3\end{aligned}$

$x=3$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Write as a single fraction  $\frac{2}{3x}+\frac{4}{5x}-\frac{9}{10x}$

Give your answer in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *First we need the lowest common denominator (lcd) of 3**x**, 5**x** and 10**x**. *

> *All already have a factor of **x**, so focus on the 3, 4 and 5. (5 and 10 both have a factor of 5)*

$\mathrm{lcd} \mathrm{of}3x,5x\mathrm{and}10x=30x$

> *Rewrite each fraction over the lcd.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3 x} & = & \frac{2 \times 10}{30 x} = \frac{20}{30 x} \\ \frac{4}{5 x} & = & \frac{4 \times 6}{30 x} = \frac{24}{30 x} \\ \frac{9}{10 x} & = & \frac{9 \times 3}{30 x} = \frac{27}{30 x}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Now add/subtract the fractions over a the single (lcd) denominator.*

$\frac{20+24-27}{30x}=\frac{17}{30x}$

> *This cannot be simplified.*

$\therefore\frac{2}{3x}+\frac{4}{5x}-\frac{9}{10x}=\frac{17}{30x}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Simplify  $\frac{2^{n}-1}{4^{n}-1}$
parts.solutionMd:
*To simpfy we are usually looking for factors.*

*There is nothing we can do with the numerator; 2 is a prime number.*

> *However we can manipulate 4*<sup>*n*</sup>* using the laws of indices.*

> *Rewrite 4 as 2*<sup>*2*</sup>* and use the law of indices "*$\left(a^{m}\right)^{n} = a^{m n}$*".*

$\frac{2^{n} - 1}{\left(2^{2}\right)^{n} - 1} = \frac{2^{n} - 1}{\left(2^{n}\right)^{2} - 1}$

> *The denominator is of the form "*$a^{2}-b^{2}$*" and so is the difference of two squares.*

$\frac{2^{n} - 1}{\left(2^{n} - 1\right) \left(2^{n} + 1\right)}$

**[1]**

> *There is now a factor of *$2^{n}-1$*on the numerator and denominator.*

$\frac{\cancel{\left(2^{n} - 1\right)}}{\cancel{\left(2^{n} - 1\right)} \left(2^{n} + 1\right)}$

$\therefore\frac{2^{n}-1}{4^{n}-1}=\frac{1}{2^{n}+1}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Solve the equation

$\frac{5}{x+2}+\frac{3}{x^{2}+2x}=2$

Show clear algebraic working.
parts.solutionMd:
> *First make a common denominator of the left-hand side of the equation. *

> *This will be the lowest common denominator (lcd) of *$x+2$* and *$x^{2}+2x$*. *

> *Spot that *$x^{2}+2x$* can be factorised as that makes the lcd easier to spot.*

$x^{2} + 2 x = x \left(x + 2\right)$ $lcd of x + 2 and x \left(x + 2\right) = x \left(x + 2\right)$

> *Rewrite the left-hand side of the equation as a single fraction over the lcd.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{x + 2} + \frac{3}{x^{2} + 2 x} & = & \frac{5 x + 3}{x \left(x + 2\right)}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Now bring the right-hand side of the equation in and multiply through by *$x \left(x + 2\right)$* to remove the fraction.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{5 x + 3}{x \left(x + 2\right)} & = & 2 \\ 5 x + 3 & = & 2 x \left(x + 2\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Expand and simplify, taking all terms to one side.*

$\begin{aligned}5 x + 3 & = & 2 x \left(x + 2\right) \\ 5 x + 3 & = & 2 x^{2} + 4 x \\ 2 x^{2} - x - 3 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Solve the resulting quadratic equation by factorising to find **x**.*

$\begin{aligned}2 x^{2} - x - 3 & = & 0 \\ \left(2 x - 3\right) \left(x + 1\right) & = & 0\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}x & = & 1 . 5 and x = - 1\end{aligned}$

$x=-1,x=1.5$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Simplify fully $\frac{10x^{2}+23x+12}{4x^{2}-9}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Both the numerator and denominator are quadratic expressions. *

> *These can be factorised but notice in particular that the denominator is the difference of two squares.*

$\frac{10 x^{2} + 23 x + 12}{4 x^{2} - 9} = \frac{\left(5 x + 4\right) \cancel{\left(2 x + 3\right)}}{\cancel{\left(2 x + 3\right)} \left(2 x - 3\right)}$

**Factorising numerator**** [1] **
**Factorising denominator**** [1]**

$\frac{5x+4}{2x-3}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
The flight of a plane was in two stages.

The table shows information about the flight.

|   | **Distance (miles)** | **Speed (mph)** | **Time (hours)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1st stage** | 731 | $x$ | $\frac{731}{x}$ |
| **2nd stage** | 287 | $x-24$ | $\frac{287}{x-24}$ |

In total, the flight lasted 2 hours. 
Work out the value of $x$.
parts.solutionMd:
*At first, this looks like it could be very complicated and involved the relationship between distance, speed and time.*

> *However, we are given the total time of the flight, so we only need be concerned with the time entries from the table.*

*The sum of the two times for each stage of the flight will be 2.* *Use this to set up an equation involving algebraic fractions.*

$\frac{731}{x}+\frac{287}{x-24}=2$

**[1]**

*To begin solving this equation, we first need to make a common denominator for the fractions on the left-hand side.*

> *The lowest common denominator (lcd) will be found by multiply **x** by (**x** - 24).*

*lcd of ***x*** and (***x*** - 24) is ***x***(***x*** - 24)*

> *Now write the left-hand side of the equation such that both fractions have the same denominator; the first will need both numerator and denominator multiplying by (**x** - 24); the second will need both multiplying by **x**.*

$\frac{731}{x} + \frac{287}{x - 24} = \frac{731 \left(x - 24\right)}{x \left(x - 24\right)} + \frac{287 x}{x \left(x - 24\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Now the left-hand side can be written as a single fraction. Expand the bracket and simplify the numerator.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{731 \left(x - 24\right)}{x \left(x - 24\right)} + \frac{287 x}{x \left(x - 24\right)} & = & \frac{731 x - 17 544 + 287 x}{x \left(x - 24\right)} \\ & = & \frac{1018 x - 17 544}{x \left(x - 24\right)}\end{aligned}$

> *Now bring in the right-hand side of the equation. *

> *To remove the fraction, multiply both sides of the equation by its denominator (**x**(**x** - 24)).*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{1018 x - 17 544}{x \left(x - 24\right)} & = & 2 \\ 1018 x - 17 544 & = & 2 x \left(x - 24\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Expand the brackets and rearrange to form a quadratic equation.*

$\begin{aligned}1018 x - 17 544 & = & 2 x^{2} - 48 x \\ 2 x^{2} - 1066 x + 17 544 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *If you spot it, divide through by 2 to make the values smaller and easier to work with.*

$x^{2}-533x+8772=0$

> *This does factorise!  But as the values are awkward you may find it easier to use the quadratic formula.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{533 \pm \sqrt{\left(- 533\right)^{2} - 4 \left(1\right) \left(8772\right)}}{2} \\ x & = & \frac{533 \pm 499}{2} \\ x & = & 516 or x = 17\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Looking at the speed column, x = 17 would give a negative speed for the 2nd stage of the flight. *

> *This is nonsense, so reject the answer x = 17.*

$\thereforex=516$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Simplify fully $\frac{x^{5}-4x^{3}}{3x-6}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Start by factorising the numerator and/or denominator.*

> *The numerator has a factor of **x*<sup>*3*</sup>* and the denominator has a factor of 3.*

$\frac{x^{5} - 4 x^{3}}{3 x - 6} = \frac{x^{3} \left(x^{2} - 4\right)}{3 \left(x - 2\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Beware! The numerator can still be factorised further; (**x*<sup>*2*</sup>* - 4) is the difference of two squares.*

$\frac{x^{3} \left(x^{2} - 4\right)}{3 \left(x - 2\right)} = \frac{x^{3} \left(x + 2\right) \left(x - 2\right)}{3 \left(x - 2\right)}$

**[1]**

> *The (**x** - 2) terms now cancel.*

$\therefore\frac{x^{5}-4x^{3}}{3x-6}=\frac{x^{3}(x+2)}{3}$* ***[1] **

**Equivalent expressions such as **$\frac{x^{4}}{3}+\frac{2x^{3}}{3}$** are allowed.**

parts.problemMd:
Show that, for $x\neq--1$

$\frac{8x^{2}-8}{4x+4}$ simplifies to the form $ax+b$       where $a$ and $b$ are integers.
parts.solutionMd:
*Start by factorising the numerator and/or denominator.*

> *The numerator has a factor of 8 and the denominator has a factor of 4.*

$\frac{8 x^{2} - 8}{4 x + 4} = \frac{8 \left(x^{2} - 1\right)}{4 \left(x + 1\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Beware! *

> *The numerator can still be factorised further; (**x*<sup>*2*</sup>* - 1) is the difference of two squares.*

$\frac{8 \left(x^{2} - 1\right)}{4 \left(x + 1\right)} = \frac{8 \left(x + 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)}{4 \left(x + 1\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Now simplify the fraction by cancelling common factors. *

> *There are common factors of 4 and (**x** + 1) on the numerator and denominator.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{\begin{matrix}2 \\ \bcancel{8} \cancel{\left(x + 1\right)} \left(x - 1\right)\end{matrix}}{\begin{matrix}\bcancel{4} \cancel{\left(x + 1\right)} \\ 1\end{matrix}} & = & \frac{2 \left(x - 1\right)}{1} \\ & = & 2 \left(x - 1\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Finally, expand the bracket to get the final answer in the correct form.*

$\therefore\frac{8x^{2}-8}{4x+4}=2x-2$*,  ***i.e.**** a ****= 2, ****b**** = -2*** ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Simplify  $\frac{25a}{8}\times\frac{2a}{5}$

Give your answer as a single fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
*To multiply fractions, we multiply numerators, then denominators.*

> *If we can spot any common factors on the. numerator and denominator first, whether they be letters or numbers, the multiplication can be easier.*

*25 and 5 share a common factor 5* 
*2 and 8 share a common factor 2*

$\frac{\begin{matrix}5 \\ \cancel{25} a\end{matrix}}{\begin{matrix}\cancel{8} \\ 4\end{matrix}} \times \frac{\begin{matrix}1 \\ \cancel{2} a\end{matrix}}{\begin{matrix}\cancel{5} \\ 1\end{matrix}}$

> *Be careful if there is lots of crossing out and if it helps, rewrite the simplified fractions, then multiply.*

$\frac{5a}{4}\timesa=\frac{5a^{2}}{4}$

> *This cannot be simplified and is a single fraction.*

$\therefore\frac{25a}{8}\times\frac{2a}{5}=\frac{5a^{2}}{4}$

**Correct single fraction but not in its simplest form**** [1] **
**Fully correct**** [1]**

**You can multiply first and simplify after if you prefer.**

parts.problemMd:
Solve  $\frac{x}{x+4}+\frac{7}{x-2}=1$

You **must** show your working.

parts.solutionMd:
*To remove a fraction, we multiply both sides of the equation by its denominator.*

> *So first, multiply both sides of the equation by (**x** + 4) to remove the first fraction on the left-hand side.*

$x + \frac{7 \left(x + 4\right)}{x - 2} = \left(x + 4\right)$

> *Next multiply both sides by (**x** - 2) to remove the other fraction.*

$x \left(x - 2\right) + 7 \left(x + 4\right) = \left(x + 4\right) \left(x - 2\right)$

**For **$x(x-2)or7(x+4)$** [1] **
**For full correct equation**** [1]**

parts.problemMd: Show that $\frac{x+9}{x^{2}-1}+\frac{4}{x+1}$ can be written in the form $\frac{a}{x-1}$ where $a$ is an integer.
parts.solutionMd:
> *First spot that x2 - 1 is the difference of two squares.*

$x^{2} - 1 = \left(x + 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)$

> *We now require the lowest common denominator of (**x** + 1)(**x** - 1) and (**x** + 1).*

*lowest common denominator is** *$\left(x + 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)$

> *The first fraction already has this denominator (in completed square form) so we need to multiply the numerator and denominator of the second fraction by (**x** - 1).*

$\frac{x + 9}{\left(x + 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)} + \frac{4 \left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x + 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Write as one single fraction over the common denominator. *

> *Add the numerators.*

$\frac{x + 9 + 4 \left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x + 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)}$

> *Expand the brackets in the numerator.*

$\frac{x + 9 + 4 x - 4}{\left(x + 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)}$

**[1]*** *

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator.*

$\frac{5 x + 5}{\left(x + 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)}$

> *The numerator factorises.*

$\frac{5 \left(x + 1\right)}{\left(x + 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)}$

**[1]**

> *There is now a factor of (**x** + 1) on both the numerator and the denominator, so these cancel.*

$\frac{x+9}{x^{2}-1}+\frac{4}{x+1}=\frac{5}{x-1},i.e.a=5$* ***[1***]*

parts.problemMd:
Show that, for $x\neq0$

$\frac{x+4}{3x}-\frac{5}{2x}$

can be written in the form  $\frac{ax+b}{cx}$ where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Fractions need a common denominator before they can be subtracted. *

> *3**x** and 2**x** already share a factor of x, so their lowest common denominator (lcd) will come from finding 3 × 2.*

*lcd of 3***x*** and 2***x*** is 6***x**

> *Now rewrite the fractions with the common denominator.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{x + 4}{3 x} - \frac{5}{2 x} & = & \frac{2 \left(x + 4\right)}{6 x} - \frac{3 \times 5}{6 x}\end{aligned}$

**One correct fraction**** [1] **
**Both correct**** [1]**

> *Now we can write this as a single fraction, subtracting the numerators.*

$\frac{2 \left(x + 4\right)}{6 x} - \frac{3 \times 5}{6 x} = \frac{2 \left(x + 4\right) - 15}{6 x}$

> *Expand and simplify the numerator.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{2 \left(x + 4\right) - 15}{6 x} & = & \frac{2 x + 8 - 15}{6 x} \\ & = & \frac{2 x - 7}{6 x}\end{aligned}$

> *Nothing else can be factorised/simplified/cancelled.*

$\frac{x+4}{3x}-\frac{5}{2x}=\frac{2x-7}{6x}$**,  i.e. ****a**** = 2, ****b**** = -7, ****c**** = 6**** [1]**

parts.problemMd:
Solve $\frac{x}{4}-\frac{2x}{x+2}=1$

Give your solutions to 2 decimal places. 
You **must** show your working.
parts.solutionMd:
*Start by making a common denominator on the left-hand side.* *To do this we need the lowest common denominator (lcd) of 4 and (**x** + 2).*

> *This can be found by multiplying them together.*

*lcd of 4 and (***x*** + 2) is 4(***x*** + 2)*

*Rewrite both fractions with the common denominator.*

> *The first fraction will need its numerator multiplying by (**x** + 2) and the second fraction by 4.*

$\frac{x}{4} - \frac{2 x}{x + 2} = \frac{x \left(x + 2\right)}{4 \left(x + 2\right)} - \frac{2 x \times 4}{4 \left(x + 2\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Write as a single fraction over the common denominator;  expand and simplify the numerator.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{x \left(x + 2\right)}{4 \left(x + 2\right)} - \frac{2 x \times 4}{4 \left(x + 2\right)} & = & \frac{x^{2} + 2 x - 8 x}{4 \left(x + 2\right)} \\ & = & \frac{x^{2} - 6 x}{4 \left(x + 2\right)}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Factorise the numerator and cancel any common factors.*

$\frac{x^{2} - 6 x}{4 \left(x + 2\right)} = \frac{x \left(x - 6\right)}{4 \left(x + 2\right)}$

*There are no common factors to cancel.*

> *Bring in the right-hand side of the equation and remove the fraction by multiplying both sides of the equation by the denominator.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{x \left(x - 6\right)}{4 \left(x + 2\right)} & = & 1 \\ x \left(x - 6\right) & = & 4 \left(x + 2\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Expand and rearrange to get a quadratic equation.*

$\begin{aligned}x^{2} - 6 x & = & 4 x + 8 \\ x^{2} - 10 x - 8 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

parts.problemMd: Show that $\frac{5 x}{x + 5} + \frac{25}{x - 7} - \frac{300}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)}$ simplifies to an integer.
parts.solutionMd:
> *First we need the lowest common denominator of (**x** + 5)(**x** - 7) and (**x** + 5)(**x** - 7).*

*lowest common denominator is** *$\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)$

> *The last fraction already has this denominator so we need to multiply the numerator and denominator of the first fraction by (**x** + 5) and similarly for the second fraction by (**x** - 7).*

$\frac{5 x \left(x - 7\right)}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)} + \frac{25 \left(x + 5\right)}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)} - \frac{300}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)}$

**Common denominator**** [1] **
**Both of the first two numerators**** [1]**

> *Write as one single fraction over the common denominator. Add/subtract the numerators accordingly.*

$\frac{5 x \left(x - 7\right) + 25 \left(x + 5\right) - 300}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)}$

> *Expand the brackets in the numerator.*

$\frac{5 x^{2} - 35 x + 25 x + 125 - 300}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator.*

$\frac{5 x^{2} - 10 x - 175}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)}$

**[1]**

> *The numerator factorises.  Taking a factor of 5 out first will make the (remaining) quadratic easier to deal with.*

$\frac{5 \left(x^{2} - 2 x - 35\right)}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)} = \frac{5 \left(x - 7\right) \left(x + 5\right)}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x - 7\right)}$

**[1]**

> *There are now factors of (**x** - 7) and (**x** + 5) on both the numerator and the denominator, so these cancel.*

$\frac{5 \cancel{\left(x - 7\right)} \bcancel{\left(x + 5\right)}}{\bcancel{\left(x + 5\right)} \cancel{\left(x - 7\right)}} = 5$

$\therefore\frac{5x}{x+5}+\frac{25}{x-7}-\frac{300}{(x+5)(x-7)}=5$* ***[1***]*

*Before simplifying the fraction, look to see if the numerator or denominator can be factorised.*

> *In this case the denominator can be.*

$\frac{3 x^{2}}{6 x^{2} + 3} = \frac{3 x^{2}}{3 \left(2 x^{2} + 1\right)}$

> *We can now see there is a factor of 3 on both the numerator and denominator so these will cancel.*

$\frac{3 x^{2}}{3 \left(2 x^{2} + 1\right)} = \frac{x^{2}}{2 x^{2} + 1}$

*Nothing else can be simplified.*

> *The third option should be circled.*

| $\frac{x^{2}}{2x^{2}+3}$ | $\frac{x^{2}}{6x^{2}+1}$ | $\boxed{\frac{\mathbf{\mathit{x}}^{2}}{2 \mathbf{\mathit{x}}^{2} + 1}}$ | $\frac{1}{2}+x^{2}$ |
|---|---|---|---|

**[1]**

parts.problemMd:

$\frac{5}{x+2}+\frac{3}{x-3}=2$

$x$ = ........... or $x$ = ...........
parts.solutionMd:
> *First we need the lowest common denominator of (**x** + 2) and (**x** - 3) on the left-hand side of the equation*

*lowest common denominator is** *$\left(x + 2\right) \left(x - 3\right)$

**[1]**

> *Multiply the numerators and denominators of the fractions on the left-hand side by the factor required to create a coommon denominator.*

$\frac{5 \left(x - 3\right)}{\left(x + 2\right) \left(x - 3\right)} + \frac{3 \left(x + 2\right)}{\left(x + 2\right) \left(x - 3\right)} = 2$

> *Write the left-hand side as one single fraction over the common denominator. *

> *Expand and simplify the numerators*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{5 \left(x - 3\right) + 3 \left(x + 2\right)}{\left(x + 2\right) \left(x - 3\right)} & = & 2 \\ \frac{5 x - 15 + 3 x + 6}{\left(x + 2\right) \left(x - 3\right)} & = & 2 \\ \frac{8 x - 9}{\left(x + 2\right) \left(x - 3\right)} & = & 2\end{aligned}$

** Numerator**** [1]**

$8 x - 9 = 2 \left(x + 2\right) \left(x - 3\right)$

> *Expand the brackets, collect 'like' terms and rearrange so the equation" equals zero ".*

$\begin{aligned}8 x - 9 & = & 2 \left(x^{2} - x - 6\right) \\ 0 & = & 2 x^{2} - 2 x - 12 - 8 x + 9 \\ 2 x^{2} - 10 x - 3 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

**Method of solving quadratic**** [1]**

> *Decimals are required for the final answers.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{5}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{31}}{2} = 5 . 283 882 . . . \\ x & = & \frac{5}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{31}}{2} = - 0 . 283 882 . . .\end{aligned}$

$\thereforex=5.3\mathrm{or}x=-0.3(1d.p.)$

parts.problemMd:
Write as a single fraction in its simplest form.

$\frac{3}{x-1}+\frac{4}{x+2}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Find the lowest common denominator by multiplying (**x** - 1) by (**x** + 2).*

*lowest common denominator is (***x*** - 1) × (***x*** + 2) = (***x*** - 1)(***x*** + 2)*

> *Multiply top-and-bottom of each fraction by the factor needed to form this denominator.*

$\frac{3 \left(x + 2\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)} + \frac{4 \left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Write as one single fraction over the common denominator. Add the numerators.*

$\frac{3 \left(x + 2\right) + 4 \left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets in the numerator.*

$\frac{3 x + 6 + 4 x - 4}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)}$

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator.*

$\frac{7 x + 2}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right)}$

> *There is nothing else that factorises or cancels.*

$\therefore\frac{3}{x-1}+\frac{4}{x+2}=\frac{7x+2}{(x-1)(x+2)}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Write $\frac{5}{4 x^{2} - 25} - \left(2 x + 3\right) \div \left(\frac{4 x^{2} + 16 x + 15}{7}\right)$  as a single fraction in its simplest form.

Show clear algebraic working
parts.solutionMd:
> **[exam-tip]**
> Simplifying algebraic fraction questions are commonly written with quadratic expressions that are able to be factorised.
> 
> Recognising this early on in the question will often result in opportunities to simplify earlier on meaning fewer instances to expand double or triple brackets unnecessarily.

> *The two quadratic expressions forming part of the question can be factorised*

> $4x^{2}-25$* is a difference of two squares*

$4 x^{2} - 25 = \left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)$

> $4x^{2}+16x+15$* can be factorised into double brackets*

- *First multiply the coefficient of the *$x^{2}$* term and constant term together*

$4\times15=60$

- *List the factor pairs of this product and identify the factor pair that add up to the value of the coefficient of the *$x$* term*

$\begin{aligned}60 & = & 1 \times 60 \\ & = & 2 \times 30 \\ & = & 3 \times 20 \\ & = & 4 \times 15 \\ & = & 5 \times 12 \\ & = & 6 \times 10\end{aligned}$

*In this case *$6+10=16$* so this is the pair of values to use*

> *Split the *$x$*term of the quadratic expression into two separate terms using the selected factor pair values as coefficients of the terms*

$4x^{2}+16x+15=4x^{2}+6x+10x+15$

> *Factorise the first two terms and the last two terms of the expression separately into single brackets*

$4 x^{2} + 6 x + 10 x + 15 = 2 x \left(2 x + 3\right) + 5 \left(2 x + 3\right)$

> *The bracketed expression is the same in both parts*

> *Factor out this term*

$4 x^{2} + 16 x + 15 = \left(2 x + 3\right) \left(2 x + 5\right)$

> *Rewrite the original question with the quadratic expressions replaced with the factorised form*

$\frac{5}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)} - \left(2 x + 3\right) \div \frac{\left(2 x + 3\right) \left(2 x + 5\right)}{7}$

> *Applying the order of operations means that the division must be calculated first*

$\left(2 x + 3\right) \div \frac{\left(2 x + 3\right) \left(2 x + 5\right)}{7}$

> *Multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor is equivalent to dividing*

$\left(2 x + 3\right) \times \frac{7}{\left(2 x + 3\right) \left(2 x + 5\right)}$

**[M1]**

> *Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators to give:*

$\frac{7 \left(2 x + 3\right)}{\left(2 x + 3\right) \left(2 x + 5\right)}$

> *Simplify the fraction by dividing through by the common factor *$2x+3$

$\frac{7}{\left(2 x + 5\right)}$

> *Put this back into the question to solve the subtraction part*

$\frac{5}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)} - \frac{7}{\left(2 x + 5\right)}$

**[M1]**

> *To subtract fractions there must be a common denominator*

> $2x+5$* is already common to both denominators but *$2x-5$* is not*

> *Multiplying the second fraction by 1 in the form *$\frac{2x-5}{2x-5}$* will result in a common denominator*

$\frac{5}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)} - \frac{7}{\left(2 x + 5\right)} \times \frac{\left(2 x - 5\right)}{\left(2 x - 5\right)}$

$= \frac{5}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)} - \frac{7 \left(2 x - 5\right)}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)}$

> *Subtract the numerators now that the denominators are the same*

$\frac{5 - 7 \left(2 x - 5\right)}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)}$

**[M1]**

> *Expand and simplify the numerator*

$\frac{5 - 14 x + 35}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)} = \frac{40 - 14 x}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)}$

**[A1]**

> *Factorise the numerator to check if any further simplifying can take place*

$\frac{2 \left(20 - 7 x\right)}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)}$

> *There are no common factors of the numerator and denominator so it cannot be simplified any further*

$\frac{2 \left(20 - 7 x\right)}{\left(2 x + 5\right) \left(2 x - 5\right)}$

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any equivalent expression will get the final mark (e.g. $\frac{40-14x}{4x^{2}-25}$)

parts.problemMd:
Express as a single fraction.

$\frac{m+1}{n+1}-\frac{m}{n}$

Simplify your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Find the lowest common denominator by multiplying (**n** + 1) by **n**.*

*lowest common denominator is (***n*** + 1) × ***n*** = ***n***(***n*** + 1)*

> *Multiply top-and-bottom of each fraction by the factor needed to form this denominator.*

$\frac{\left(m + 1\right) n}{n \left(n + 1\right)} - \frac{m \left(n + 1\right)}{n \left(n + 1\right)}$

> *Write as one single fraction over the common denominator. Subtract the numerators.*

$\frac{n \left(m + 1\right) - m \left(n + 1\right)}{n \left(n + 1\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets in the numerator.*

$\frac{m n + n - m n - m}{n \left(n + 1\right)}$

> *Collect "like" terms in the numerator.*

$\frac{n - m}{n \left(n + 1\right)}$

> *Nothing else factorises or cancels.*

$\therefore\frac{m+1}{n+1}-\frac{m}{n}=\frac{n-m}{n(n+1)}$* ***[1]**

**[1]**

*Finally evaluate *$\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{- 2}$* by writing *$\frac{1}{2}$* as *$2^{-1}$* and write your final answer as simply as possible.*

> *Use your calculator if unsure for this part.*

parts.problemMd: Simplify fully   $\frac{a^{3}b^{2}}{cd}\times\frac{c}{ab^{5}}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *First express as a single fraction by multiplying and simplifying.*

$\frac{a^{3}b^{2}}{cd}\times\frac{c}{ab^{5}}=\frac{a^{3}b^{2}c}{ab^{5}cd}$

> *Separate into fractions by each letter.*

$\frac{a^{3}b^{2}c}{ab^{5}cd}=\frac{a^{3}}{a}\times\frac{b^{2}}{b^{5}}\times\frac{c}{c}\times\frac{1}{d}$

> *Cancel/simplify each fraction using the rules of indices " *$a^{m}\diva^{n}=a^{m-n}$* ".*

$\frac{a^{3}}{a}\times\frac{b^{2}}{b^{5}}\times\frac{c}{c}\times\frac{1}{d}=a^{2}\timesb^{-3}\times1\timesd^{-1}$

> *Simplify for the final answer, using the rule of indices " *$a^{-m}=\frac{1}{a^{m}}$* ".*

$a^{2}\timesb^{-3}\times1\timesd^{-1}=\frac{a^{2}}{b^{3}d}$

$\therefore\frac{a^{3}b^{2}c}{cd}\times\frac{c}{ab^{5}}=\frac{a^{2}}{b^{3}d}$ **[1]**

> *Using the law of indices *$\left(a^{m}\right)^{n}$* and working with numbers first, then letters in order, everything inside the bracket needs raising to the power of 4.*

$\left(2 x^{3} y^{5}\right)^{4} = \left(2\right)^{4} \left(x^{3}\right)^{4} \left(y^{5}\right)^{4}$

> *Use the same law of indices to simplify each part.*

$\left(2\right)^{4} \left(x^{3}\right)^{4} \left(y^{5}\right)^{4} = 16 x^{12} y^{20}$

**Final answer:** $\therefore(2x^{3}y^{5})^{4}=16x^{12}y^{20}$** **

parts.problemMd:
$\left(a r^{b}\right)^{4} = 16 r^{20}$  where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers.

Work out $a$ and $b$

parts.solutionMd:
> *Use the rule of indices " *$\left(a b\right)^{m} = a^{m} b^{m}$* " to remove the brackets from the left-hand side of the equation.*

$\left(a r^{b}\right)^{4} = a^{4} \left(r^{b}\right)^{4}$

> *Use the rule of indices " *$\left(a^{m}\right)^{n} = a^{m n}$* " to simplify the second part.*

$a^{4} \left(r^{b}\right)^{4} = a^{4} r^{4 b}$

> *We can now write down two equations; one for **a**, one for **b**.*

$\begin{aligned}a^{4} r^{4 b} & = & 16 r^{20} \\ \therefore a^{4} & = & 16 \\ and r^{4 b} & = & r^{20}\end{aligned}$

> *Solve these equations to find **a** and **b**.*

$\begin{aligned}a^{4} & = & 16 \\ \therefore a & = & \sqrt[4]{16} \\ a & = & 2\end{aligned}$

> *and*

$\begin{aligned}r^{4 b} & = & r^{20} \\ \therefore 4 b & = & 20 \\ b & = & 5\end{aligned}$

**Final answer:** $a=2,b=5$** **

**One mark for each**** [2]**

$\left(16 e^{10} f^{6}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} = \left(16\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \left(e^{10}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \left(f^{6}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$

> *Use the same law of indices to simplify each part, alongside *$\sqrt{a}=a^{\frac{1}{2}}$*.*

$\left(16\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \left(e^{10}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \left(f^{6}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} = 4 e^{5} f^{3}$

**Final answer:** $\therefore(16e^{10}f^{6})^{\frac{1}{2}}=4e^{5}f^{3}$** **

**2 out of 3 parts correct**** [1]**
** ****All correct**** [1]**

parts.problemMd: Write $2x^{2}+16x+35$ in the form $a \left(x + b\right)^{2}  +  c$ where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers.
parts.solutionMd:
> *The result required is in completed square form. As the coefficient of **x*<sup>*2 *</sup>*is not 1, begin by factorising the number 2 from the first two terms of the expression. *

$\begin{aligned}2 x^{2} + 16 x + 35 & = & 2 \left(x^{2 } + 8 x\right) + 35\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Complete the square on the expression in the brackets. *

> *Set up a squared bracket with two terms; *$x$* and half of the coefficient of the *$x$* term - in this case 4. *

> *Considering that (**x **+ 4)*<sup>*2 *</sup>*= **x*<sup>*2 *</sup>*+ 8**x** + 16, we need to subtract 16.*

$\begin{aligned}2 \left(x^{2 } + 8 x\right) + 35 & = & 2 \left[\left(x + 4\right)^{2} - 16\right] + 25\end{aligned}$

> *Multiply out the 2.*

$\begin{aligned}2 x^{2} + 16 x + 35 & = & 2 \left[\left(x + 4\right)^{2} - 16\right] + 35 \\ & = & 2 \left(x + 4\right)^{2} - 32 + 35\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned} & = & 2 \left(x + 4\right)^{2} + 3\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\mathbf{\mathit{a}} & = & 2 , \mathbf{\mathit{b}} = 4 , \mathbf{\mathit{c}} = 3\end{aligned}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Express $7+12x--3x^{2}$ in the form $a+b(x+c)^{2}$ where $a,b$ and$c$are integers.
parts.solutionMd:

> *To avoid fractions, take this factor out of the **x*<sup>*2*</sup>* and **x** terms only.*

$7 + 12 x - 3 x^{2} = 7 - 3 \left(x^{2} - 4 x\right)$

**[1]**

$7 - 3 \left(x^{2} - 4 x\right) = 7 - 3 \left[\left(x - 2\right)^{2} - 4\right]$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}7 - 3 \left[\left(x - 2\right)^{2} - 4\right] & = & 7 - 3 \left(x - 2\right)^{2} + 12 \\ & = & 19 - 3 \left(x - 2\right)^{2}\end{aligned}$

$\therefore7+12x-3x^{2}=19-3(x-2)^{2}$ **[1]**

**i.e. **$a=19,b=-3,c=-2$**.**

parts.problemMd: Write $x^{2}-18x-27$ in the form $ \left(x + k\right)^{2} + h$.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Halve the coefficient of **x **and this will be the value of **k**.*

$k=\frac{-18}{2}=-9$

**[1]**

> *Expand *$\left(x - 9\right)^{2}$* by multiplying out *$\left(x - 9\right) \left(x - 9\right) .$

$\left(x - 9\right)^{2}=x^{2} - 9x -9 x+ 81$
$\left(x - 9\right)^{2}=x^{2}-18x + 81$

> *You want the constant term to be -27 so subtract 81 from sides to get rid of the constant term. *

> *Then subtract 27 from both sides to make the constant term -27.*

$\left(x - 9\right)^{2} - 81 - 27 = x^{2} - 18 x - 27$

> *Find the value of **h** by simplifying the term at the end.*

$h=-81-27=-108$

$(x-9)^{2}-108$ **[1]**

> *Rewrite the equation using the solution from part (a).*

$\left(x - 9\right)^{2} - 108 = 0$

> *Add 108 to both sides.*

$\left(x - 9\right)^{2} = 108$

> *Square root both sides. Remember there are two values, a positive and a negative.*

$x-9=\pm\sqrt{108}$

**[1]**

> *Add 9 to both sides.*

$x=9\pm\sqrt{108}$

> *Simplify the expressions using your calculator.*

$x=9+6\sqrt{3}$** ****or**** **$x=9-6\sqrt{3}$**[1]**

**Rounding to 3sf is acceptable: **$x=19.4$** or **$x=-1.39$

parts.problemMd: Express $3x^{2}--6x+5$  in the form $a(x--b)^{2}+c$
parts.solutionMd:
**Method 1**

> *To complete the square, start by taking a factor of 3 out of the first two terms*

$3 x^{2} - 6 x + 5 = 3 \left(x^{2} - 2 x\right) + 5$

**[M1]**

> *Then complete the square on the function in the brackets*

- *Halve the coefficient of  *$x$* for the constant inside the curved brackets*
- *and subtract that value squared*

$3 \left[\left(x - 1\right)^{2} - 1^{2}\right] + 5$

**[M1]**

> *Expand the square brackets and simplify*

$= 3 ( x - 1 ) ^{2} - 3 + 5$
$=3 \left(x - 1\right)^{2} + 2$

> *That's in the form required, with *$a=3$*, *$b=1$* and *$c=2$

$3 \left(x - 1\right)^{2} + 2$

**[A1]**

**Method 2**

> *You could expand the *$a(x--b)^{2}+c$* and compare coefficients*

$\begin{aligned}a \left(x – b\right)^{2} + c & = & a \left(x^{2} - 2 b x + b^{2}\right) + c \\ & = & a x^{2} - 2 a b x + a b^{2} + c\end{aligned}$

**[M1]**

> *Set that equal to the original quadratic*

$3x^{2}-6x+5=ax^{2}-2abx+ab^{2}+c$

> *Comparing coefficients*

$a=3$

$\begin{aligned}- 2 a b & = & - 6 \\ - 2 \times 3 \times b & = & - 6 \\ b & = & 1\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}a b^{2} + c & = & 5 \\ 3 \times 1^{2} + c & = & 5 \\ c + 3 & = & 5 \\ c & = & 2\end{aligned}$

**[M1]**

$3 \left(x - 1\right)^{2} + 2$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> For Method 2:
> 
> **M1**: For expanding the expression correctly.
> 
> **M1**: For equating the coefficients of at least two of these.
> 
> **A1**: For writing the correct answer with *a*, *b* and *c* in the right places.

parts.problemMd: Show that $(x+1)(x+2)(x+3)$ can be written in the form $ax^{3}+bx^{2}+cx+d$ where  $a,b,c$ and $d$ are positive integers.
parts.solutionMd:
*Expand the last two brackets (by multiplying all terms in the second bracket by all terms in the third bracket)*

$\left(x + 2\right) \left(x + 3\right) = x^{2} + 2 x + 3 x + 6$

**3 out of 4 terms correct**** [1]**

*Collect the "like" **x** terms*

$x^{2}+5x+6$

> *Put the result above in brackets and multiply it by the first (unused) bracket  *

> $\left(x + 1\right) \left(x^{2} + 5 x + 6\right)$*  *

> *Expand these brackets (by multiplying all terms in the first bracket by all terms in the second)  *

$x^{3}+5x^{2}+6x+x^{2}+5x+6$

**4 out of 6 terms correct**** [1]**

> *Collect the "like" **x*<sup>*2*</sup>* and **x** terms  *

> $x^{3}+6x^{2}+11x+6$*  *

> *This is now in the form *$ax^{3}+bx^{2}+cx+d$* where **a** = 1, **b** = 6, **c** = 11 and **d** = 6 (all positive whole numbers)*

$x^{3}+6x^{2}+11x+6$ **[1]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> In a 'show that' question you must write out every expansion step; stating only the final answer or the values of a, b, c and d scores no marks.

parts.problemMd: Simplify fully $\left(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{4 b} \right) \left(\sqrt{a} - 2 \sqrt{b}\right)$
parts.solutionMd:
*Method 1*

*Expand the brackets (by multiplying all terms in the first bracket by all terms in the second)* * *

$\sqrt{a \\times \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{a} \\times ( - 2 \sqrt{b} ) + \sqrt{4} b} \\times \sqrt{a + \sqrt{4} b} \\times ( - 2 \sqrt{b} )$
$= \sqrt{a \sqrt{a} - 2 \sqrt{a} \sqrt{b} + \sqrt{4} b} \sqrt{a - 2 \sqrt{4} b} \sqrt{b}$ * *

*Simplify *$\sqrt{4b}$* using the surd rule that *$\sqrt{xy}=\sqrt{x}\sqrt{y}$ * *

$\sqrt{4b}=\sqrt{4}\sqrt{b}=2\sqrt{b}$

**[1]**

*Replace *$\sqrt{4b}$*with *$2\sqrt{b}$*in the expansion above and cancel the middle terms* * *

$\sqrt{a} \sqrt{a} - \cancel{2 \sqrt{a} \sqrt{b} } + \cancel{2 \sqrt{b} \sqrt{a} } - 4 \sqrt{b} \sqrt{b}$
$=\sqrt{a} \sqrt{a}-4\sqrt{b} \sqrt{b}$ * *

*Simplify *$\sqrt{a}\sqrt{a}$* using the surd rule that *$\sqrt{x} \sqrt{x} = \left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{2} = x$ * *

$\sqrt{a}\sqrt{a}=a$

**[1]**

> *Replace *$\sqrt{a}\sqrt{a}$* with *$a$* and *$\sqrt{b}\sqrt{b}$* with *$b$* in the expansion*

$a-4b$* ***[1]**

> *Method 2*

*Simplify *$\sqrt{4b}$* using the surd rule that *$\sqrt{xy}=\sqrt{x}\sqrt{y}$ * *

$\sqrt{4b}=\sqrt{4}\sqrt{b}=2\sqrt{b}$

**[1]**

*Replace *$\sqrt{4b}$*with *$2\sqrt{b}$*in the question* * *

$\left(\sqrt{a} + 2 \sqrt{b}\right) \left(\sqrt{a} - 2 \sqrt{b}\right)$ * *

*This is the "difference of two squares", (**p** + **q**)(**p** - **q**) = **p*<sup>*2*</sup>* - **q*<sup>*2*</sup> *Use the "difference of two squares" to expand the brackets* * *

$\left(\sqrt{a}\right)^{2} - \left(2 \sqrt{b}\right)^{2}$ * *

*Square the terms* * *

$a-2^{2}b$

**[1]**

$a-4b$**[1]**

parts.problemMd: Solve           $\left(1 - x\right)^{2} < \frac{9}{25}$
parts.solutionMd:
*This is a quadratic inequality question*

*Method 1*

*Expand the brackets on the left, by writing it as (1 - **x**)(1 - **x**)* * *

$1-2x+x^{2}<\frac{9}{25}$ * *

*Multiply both sides by 25* * *

$25-50x+25x^{2}<9$ * *

*Subtract 9 from both sides* * *

$16-50x+25x^{2}<0$

**[1]*** *

*Reorder the terms* * *

$25x^{2}-50x+16<0$ * *

*Either "see" the factorisation or use solutions from a calculator that solves quadratic equations to skip to the next line* * *

$\left(5 x - 8\right) \left(5 x - 2\right) < 0$

*Find the critical points (the values of **x** that make each bracket zero)* * *

$\frac{8}{5}$* **and** *$\frac{2}{5}$

**[1]*** *

*These are the **x**-intercepts of the positive quadratic graph *$y = \left(5 x - 8\right) \left(5 x - 2\right)$

> *Find where the graph is below the **x**-axis, "< 0"*

*between the ***x***-intercepts*

$\frac{2}{5}<x<\frac{8}{5}$** [1]**

*Method 2*

*See that if *$a^{2}<\frac{9}{25}$* then *$a$* must be any number between *$-\frac{3}{5}<a<\frac{3}{5}$* (as "squaring" this part of the number line gives values that are <*$\frac{9}{25}$*)* * *

$-\frac{3}{5}<1-x<\frac{3}{5}$

**[1]*** *

*Multiply both sides by -1 (this will flip the inequality signs too)* * *

$\frac{3}{5}>-1+x>-\frac{3}{5}$ * *

*Add 1 to both sides* * *

$1+\frac{3}{5}>x>-\frac{3}{5}+1\,\frac{8}{5}>x>\frac{2}{5}$

**adding 1 to both sides ****[1]*** *

> *Write with the inequality signs the standard way round*

$\frac{2}{5}<x<\frac{8}{5}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
![q5-hard-2-3-expanding-brackets-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/algebra/expanding-brackets/assets/001-q5-hard-2-3-expanding-brackets-edexcel-gcse-math.png)

The area of square $ABCD$ is $10$ cm<sup>2</sup>.

Show that $x^{2}+6x=1$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Method 1*

> *Add the two parts together to write down an expression for the side of the square.*

$AB=AD=3+x$

> *The total area of the square will be this expression squared. Form an expression for the total area of the square.*

$Total area = \left(3 + x\right)^{2}$

** ****[1]**

> *Expand the brackets, remember to multiply each term in the first by each term in the second.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(3 + x\right) \left(3 + x\right) & = & 9 + 3 x + 3 x + x^{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify.*

$\begin{aligned}Total area & = & x^{2} + 6 x + 9 \end{aligned}$

> *Form an equation by setting this equal to 10.*

$\begin{aligned}x^{2} + 6 x + 9 & = & 10\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Reach the equation given in the question by subtracting 9 from each side.*

$\begin{aligned}x^{2} + 6 x + 9 & = & 10 \\ - 9 & = & - 9 \\ x^{2} + 6 x & = & 1\end{aligned}$

$x^{2}+6x=1$** [1]**

> *Method 2*

> *Write down an expression for the area of each part of the square individually.*

![lI_QDSbV_2-10-forming-and-solving-equations-easy-q5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-modular-24-higher-unit-1/algebra/expanding-brackets/assets/002-li-qdsbv-2-10-forming-and-solving-equations-easy.png)

**At least two correct ****[1]**

> *The total area of the square will be the total of these four areas added together. *

> *Form an expression for the total area of the square.*

$\mathrm{Total} \mathrm{area}=9+3x+3x+x^{2}$

> *Form an equation by setting the total area equal to 10.*

$\begin{aligned}9 + 3 x + 3 x + x^{2} & = & 10\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify.*

$\begin{aligned}x^{2} + 6 x + 9 & = & 10\end{aligned}$

> *Reach the equation given in the question by subtracting 9 from each side.*

$\begin{aligned}x^{2} + 6 x + 9 & = & 10 \\ - 9 & = & - 9 \\ x^{2} + 6 x & = & 1\end{aligned}$

$x^{2}+6x=1$** [1]**
